old_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, Bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the off and leg stump. 16
new_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side. Bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the off and leg stump.

old_digest: When a wide is called the ball does not become “dead” and the batsman may be out stumped or run out.
new_digest: When a wide is called the ball does not on that account become “dead” and the batsman may be out stumped or run out.

old_digest: If runs are made off a “No Ball,” although the runs are scored and not the “No Ball,” the bowler is allowed another delivery. If one run is attempted and the batsman is run out the “No Ball” alone counts.
new_digest: If one run is attempted and the batsman is run out the “No Ball” alone counts If runs are made off a “No Ball,” although the runs are scored and not the “No Ball,” the bowler is allowed another delivery.

old_digest: If the ball rebounds off the pads or person of the wicket-keeper, without having first touched the bat or hand of the Striker, and the Striker is out of his ground the decision should be “Stumped,” and not “Run Out.” 10 It is sufficient for the wicket-keeper to remove one bail in order to run out or stump a batsman.
new_digest: Notes on Law 23 If the ball rebounds off the pads or person of the wicket-keeper, without having first touched the bat or hand of the Striker, and the Striker is out of his ground the decision should be “Stumped,” and not “Run Out.” It is sufficient for the wicket-keeper to remove one bail in order to run out or stump a batsman.

old_digest: A Batsman may be out l b w, although the bowler is bowling round the wicket, if the case comes within this Law.
new_digest: A Batsman may be out lbw, although the bowler is bowling round the wicket, if the case comes within this Law.

old_digest: It is sometimes only possible for a bowler bowling round the wicket to obtain an l b w with a breaking ball.
new_digest: It is sometimes only possible for a bowler bowling round the wicket to obtain an lbw with a breaking ball.

old_digest: If in running, or at any other time, when the ball is in play he be out of bis ground, and his wicket be struck down by the hall after touching any fieldsman, or by the hand or arm, with ball in hand, of any fieldsman—“Run out.” It would not be out if the striker hit the ball into the opposite wickets —the other batsman being out of his ground—unless the nail had been touched by a fieldsman after being hit and before striking the wickets.
new_digest: If in running, or at any other time, when the ball is in play he be out of his ground, and his wicket be struck down by the ball after touching any fieldsman, or by the hand or arm, with ball in hand, of any fieldsman;—“ Run out.” It would not be out if the striker hit the ball into the opposite wickets—the other batsman being out of his ground—unless the bail had been touched by a fieldsman after being hit and before striking the wickets.

old_digest: It should be noted, especially in League and Saturday Matches, that Umpires are appointed “one for each end” and not one for each side. 6
new_digest: It should be noted, especially in League and Saturday Matches, that Umpires are appointed “one for each end” and not one for each side.

old_digest: When a run has been made off a no-ball the no-ball should be scored although the ball has been caught. 12
new_digest: When a run has been made off a no-ball the no-ball should be scored although the ball has been caught.

old_digest: A bowler may run a Batsman out, without having delivered the ball, in anyway authorized by the Laws, he may have passed the bowling crease in his run or may change the ball from one hand to the other before throwing at the wicket or knocking off the bails.
new_digest: A bowler may run a Batsman out, without having delivered the ball, in anyway authorized by the Laws. He may have passed the bowling crease in his run or may change the ball from one hand to the other before throwing at the wicket or knocking off the bails.

old_digest: No act on the part of the fielding side can cause a batsman to be out after the Umpire has called “Over,” but an appeal may be made within the allotted time. 15
new_digest: No act on the part of the fielding side can cause a batsman to be out after the Umpire has called “Over,” but an appeal may be made within the allotted time.

old_digest: The In-side may declare their innings at an end in a three days’ match, at or after the luncheon interval on the second day; in a two days’ match the Captain of the batting side has power to declare his innings at a close at any time; but such declaration may not be made on the first day later than 1 hour and 40 minutes before the hour agreed on for drawing stumps; in a one day match at any time.
new_digest: The In-side may declare their innings at an end in a three days’ match, at any time on the second day: in a two days’ match the Captain of the batting side has power to declare his innings at a close at any time; but such declaration may not be made on the first day later than 1 hour and 40 minutes before the hour agreed on for drawing stumps; in a one day match at any time.

Pending an alteration to this Law the M.C.C. have advised the County Cricket Clubs to concur in the following procedure to adopt any covering to protect the ground against rain at any time after 7 o’clock a.m. on the morning of the first day of a match. After the actual commencement of play the ground may be again protected when necessary and shall be protected every night during the continuation of a match, but the covering shall be removed each morning, if fine, at 7 o’clock a.m. The covering must not protect a larger area than 18ft by 12ft at each end, and must not protect more than 3ft 6in in front of the popping crease. --2 7
